title: Designing more efficient quantum circuits with Claude
key_facts: Anthropic gave Claude plain-language specifications for eight quantum circuits drawn from chemistry, optimization, physics simulation and number theory, plus an automated evaluator that checks and scores each design.

Claude Mythos 5 worked in a closed loop (propose a design, get a score, improve) with no human input between rounds, and found designs that improve on the best published circuits, in some cases by an order of magnitude or more.

Elliptic-curve point addition: after 53 hours with minimal human input, Claude found a way to run the divsteps modular-inversion method without storing its branch history; one design in the new family uses 12% more qubits but 17x fewer gates than the smallest previous design.

Quantum optimisation (decoded quantum interferometry): Claude switched the decoder to Berlekamp-Massey decoding and cut the decoder's gate count by a factor of 12 relative to Google's previous construction.
Claude checked its divsteps design with large-scale numerical simulations and formal proofs in Lean; the optimisation decoder fails about one run in 10,000, within the error rate the task allows.

Context given in the post: the gate estimate for simulating FeMoco (a nitrogen-fixing enzyme core) fell from about 50 trillion Toffoli gates in 2017 to about 340 million, a roughly 150,000-fold reduction that took many research groups eight years.

Limitation reported: Claude was conservative by nature, repeatedly second-guessing improvements and preferring well-known approaches, so the team required several qualitatively different approaches in parallel and occasionally prompted it to broaden its search.

The work was led by Andi Gu in Anthropic's STEM Fellows Program, mentored by Alek Kemeny, a quantum physicist at Anthropic, in collaboration with Harvard University researchers; the full paper is on arXiv.
quote_evidence: Working largely on its own, Claude found designs that improve on the best published circuits, in some cases by an order of magnitude or more.
Compared with the smallest previous design, one circuit in the family uses 12% more qubits but 17x fewer gates.
Together, these optimizations reduced the number of gates in the decoder by a factor of 12 relative to Google’s previous construction.
why_it_matters_hint: Anthropic says cheaper circuits cut the quantum resources useful applications need, so practical quantum computers could arrive sooner than expected.
event_date: 16 Oct 2026 (post published; the 53-hour run date is not stated)
notes: Anthropic is reporting on its own model; results are in an arXiv paper and no outside review is reported in the post. Scoring was done by an evaluator the team supplied. Full text read from anthropic.com (HTTP 200).
